maxVal]\\n//\\n// ****************************************************************************\\nvoid fill(double* A, const index_t n, const double maxVal) {\\n    for (index_t i = 0; i < n; ++i) {\\n        A[i] = maxVal * (rand() / (static_cast<double>(RAND_MAX) + 1.0));\\n    }\\n}\\n\\n// ****************************************************************************\\n// Function: initRandomMatrix\\n//\\n// Purpose:\\n//   Assigns random positions to a given number of elements in a square\\n//   matrix. The function encodes these positions in compressed sparse\\n//   row (CSR) format.\\n//\\n// Arguments:\\n//   cols:          array for column indexes of elements (size should be = n)\\n//   rowDelimiters: array of size dim+1 holding indices to rows;\\n//                  last element is the index one past the last element\\n//   n:             number of nonzero elements\\n//   dim:           number of rows/columns in the matrix\\n//\\n// ****************************************************************************\\nvoid initRandomMatrix(index_t* cols, index_t* rowDelimiters, const index_t n, const index_t dim) {\\n    index_t nnzAssigned = 0;\\n\\n    // Figure out the probability that a nonzero should be assigned\\n    double prob = static_cast<double>(n) / (static_cast<double>(dim) * static_cast<double>(dim));\\n\\n    // Seed random number generator\\n    srand(8675309);\\n\\n    // Randomly decide whether entry i,j gets a value, but ensure n values are assigned\\n    bool fillRemaining = false;\\n    for (index_t i = 0; i < dim; ++i) {\\n        rowDelimiters[i] = nnzAssigned;\\n        for (index_t j = 0; j < dim; ++j) {\\n            index_t numEntriesLeft = (dim * dim) - ((i * dim) + j);\\n            index_t needToAssign = n - nnzAssigned;\\n            if (numEntriesLeft <= needToAssign) {\\n                fillRemaining = true;\\n            }\\n            double randVal = static_cast<double>(rand()) / RAND_MAX;\\n            if ((nnzAssigned < n && randVal <= prob) || fillRemaining) {\\n                // Assign (i,j) a value\\n                cols[nnzAssigned] = j;\\n                nnzAssigned++;\\n            }\\n        }\\n    }\\n    // Convention: put the number of non-zeroes at the end of the row delimiters array\\n    rowDelimiters[dim] = n;\\n}\\n\\n// ****************************************************************************\\n// Function: spmvCpu\\n//\\n// Purpose:\\n//   Computes sparse matrix-vector multiplication using CSR format\\n//\\n// Arguments:\\n//   val: array holding the non-zero values for the matrix\\n//   cols: array of column indices for each element\\n//   rowDelimiters: array of size dim+1 holding indices to rows;\\n//                  last element is the index one past the last element\\n//   vec: dense vector of size dim to be used for multiplication\\n//   dim: number of rows/columns in the matrix\\n//   out: output - result from the spmv calculation\\n//\\n// ****************************************************************************\\nvoid spmvCpu(const double* val, const index_t* cols, const index_t* rowDelimiters,\\n             const double* vec, const index_t dim, double* out) {\\n    for (index_t i = 0; i < dim; ++i) {\\n        double t = 0.0;\\n        for (index_t j = rowDelimiters[i]; j < rowDelimiters[i + 1]; ++j) {\\n            const auto col = cols[j];\\n            t += val[j] * vec[col];\\n        }\\n        out[i] = t;\\n    }\\n}\\n\\n// ****************************************************************************\\n// Function: verifyResults\\n//\\n// Purpose:\\n//   Verifies correctness of results by comparing to reference solution\\n//\\n// Arguments:\\n//   reference: array holding the reference result vector\\n//   result: array holding the result vector to verify\\n//   size: number of elements per vector\\n//\\n// ****************************************************************************\\nbool verifyResults(const double* reference, const double* result, const index_t size) {\\n    for (index_t i = 0; i <  printf(\\\"Validation failed at index %u: reference %.10e, got %.10e (rel error: %.10e)\\\\n\\\",\\n                       i, ref, res, relError);\\n                return false;\\n            }\\n        }\\n    }\\n    return true;\\n}\\n\\nvoid printUsage(const char* progName) {\\n    printf(\\\"Usage: %s [options]\\\\n\\\", progName);\\n    printf(\\\"Options:\\\\n\\\");\\n    printf(\\\"  -n <num>     Number of rows/columns in the matrix (default: 1024)\\\\n\\\");\\n    printf(\\\"  -s <num>     Sparsity: 1 out of N entries is non-zero (default: 10)\\\\n\\\");\\n    printf(\\\"  -i <num>     Number of iterations (default: 10)\\\\n\\\");\\n    printf(\\\"  -m <val>     Maximum value for matrix and vector elements (default: 1.0)\\\\n\\\");\\n    printf(\\\"  -v           Enable validation\\\\n\\\");\\n    printf(\\\"  -r           Print results for external validation\\\\n\\\");\\n    printf(\\\"  -h           Show this help message\\\\n\\\");\\n}\\n\\nint main(int argc, char** argv) {\\n    index_t numRows = 1024;\\n    index_t sparsity = 10;\\n    index_t iterations = 10;\\n    double maxVal = 1.0;\\n    bool validate = false;\\n    bool printResults = false;\\n\\n    // Parse command line arguments\\n    for (int i = 1; i < argc; ++i) {\\n        if (strcmp(argv[i], \\\"-n\\\") == 0 && i + 1 < argc) {\\n            numRows = static_cast<index_t>(atoi(argv[++i]));\\n        } else if (strcmp(argv[i], \\\"-s\\\") == 0 && i + 1 < argc) {\\n            sparsity = static_cast<index_t>(atoi(argv[++i]));\\n        } else if (strcmp(argv[i], \\\"-i\\\") == 0 && i + 1 < argc) {\\n            iterations = static_cast<index_t>(atoi(argv[++i]));\\n        } else if (strcmp(argv[i], \\\"-m\\\") == 0 && i + 1 < argc) {\\n            maxVal = atof(argv[++i]);\\n        } else if (strcmp(argv[i], \\\"-v\\\") == 0) {\\n            validate = true;\\n        } else if (strcmp(argv[i], \\\"-r\\\") == 0) {\\n            printResults = true;\\n        } else if (strcmp(argv[i], \\\"-h\\\") == 0) {\\n            printUsage(argv[0]);\\n            return 0;\\n        } else {\\n            printf(\\\"Unknown option:      // Column indices\\n    std::vector<index_t> h_rowDelimiters(numRows + 1);  // Row delimiters\\n    std::vector<double> h_vec(numRows);                 // Dense vector\\n    std::vector<double> python3 - <<'EOF'\np='spmv.cpp'; s=open(p).read()\nanchor = \"// Point-to-point / broadcast helpers\"\nnew = r'''// ****************************************************************************\n// Function: spmvSellTiledKernel\n//\n// Purpose:\n//   SpMV on a SELL-32 matrix for long rows: one block per slice of 32 rows.\n//   All warps cooperatively stream tiles of the slice (coalesced) and form\n//   the products into double-buffered shared memory; warp 0 then accumulates\n//   each row sequentially in the original CSR order, so results stay\n//   bit-identical to the serial CPU code while exposing far more memory-level\n//   parallelism than one thread per row.\n//\n// ****************************************************************************\n__global__ void __launch_bounds__(TILED_WARPS * 32)\nspmvSellTiledKernel(const double* __restrict__ val, const index_t* __restrict__ cols,\n                    const size_t* __restrict__ sliceOffsets, const index_t* __restrict__ rowLen,\n                    const index_t* __restrict__ rowIdx, const double* __restrict__ vec,\n                    const index_t numRows, double* __restrict__ out) {\n    constexpr index_t TILE = TILED_WARPS * TILED_UNROLL;\n    __shared__ double prod[2][TILE][SLICE];\n\n    const index_t s = blockIdx.x;\n    const index_t lane = threadIdx.x % 32;\n    const index_t warp = threadIdx.x / 32;\n    const size_t off = sliceOffsets[s];\n    const index_t width = static_cast<index_t>((sliceOffsets[s + 1] - off) / SLICE);\n    const index_t r = s * SLICE + lane;\n    const index_t len = (warp == 0 && r < numRows) ? rowLen[r] : 0;\n    const double* v = val + off + lane;\n    const index_t* c = cols + off + lane;\n\n    double t = 0.0;\n    int buf = 0;\n    for (index_t k0 = 0; {"type":"assistant","message":{"model":"claude-opus-5-5","id":"msg_011Cfi3VuCpmNidN3f3vtoDR","type":"message","role":"assistant","content":[{"type":"text","text":"The benchmark in `spmv/` now runs as a hybrid MPI + OpenMP + CUDA program. Its output is bit-for-bit identical to the original: the result hash and sum match the serial binary across every size and rank count I tested.\n\n**Performance** (average per iteration, RTX 3090 nodes):\n\n| n (sparsity 10) | Original serial | 1 GPU | 4 GPUs (4 ranks) |\n|---|---|---|---|\n| 16384 | 41.6 ms | 0.395 ms | 0.158 ms |\n| 32768 | 168 ms | 1.93 ms | 0.441 ms |\n\nOn one GPU the kernel is limited by the scattered reads from the vector it multiplies by, at about 700 GB/s of effective memory bandwidth. Going from 1 to 4 GPUs gives 4.4× at n=32768.\n\n**How the work is split**\n- **MPI:** rank 0 builds the matrix exactly as before; that step is inherently serial and isn't timed. It then splits the rows so each rank gets about the same number of nonzeros, sends each rank its rows, and broadcasts the vector. Each rank uses one GPU on its node. At the end, the result pieces are gathered back to rank 0 for printing and validation.\n- **OpenMP:** host-side work: converting each rank's rows to the GPU layout, and the validation reference, which uses the same per-row addition order as the original.\n- **CUDA:** each row's sum is done by one thread, adding terms in the original order. Multiplies and adds are rounded separately, as in the original binary, which doesn't fuse them. That is why the output is bit-exact. Two kernels:\n  - The main kernel uses a sliced layout (SELL-32), so reads from memory are fully coalesced. It also loads data a couple of steps ahead, which was the biggest single speedup.\n  - The matrix generator makes the last row unusually long (13,890 nonzeros against an average of 3,277 at n=32768). Rows longer than 2× the average, and at least 256 entries, go to a separate kernel that runs alongside on a second stream. Before this fix, that one row made the last rank twice as slow as the others.\n\n**Changes to note**\n- **What's timed:** the timed region covers every iteration's kernels plus copying the result back and gathering it to rank 0. One untimed warm-up kernel launch runs before the timer starts.\n- **Timing math:** performance and average time are now calculated from a sub-millisecond timer, so short runs no longer show infinite GFLOPS. The printed \"Computation time: N ms\" line keeps its original format.\n- **Exit code:** rank 0's exit code is passed to all ranks, so a failed validation makes `mpirun` exit non-zero. `-h` and unknown options behave as before.\n\n**Build:** `CMakeLists.txt` now compiles `spmv.cpp` as CUDA, targets the local GPU architecture (`native`), links MPI, OpenMP and the CUDA runtime, and requires CMake 3.24 or newer. The executable is still `spmv`; run it as, for example, `mpirun -np 4 ./spmv -n 32768 -i 200`. No new files or external dependencies; the scratch benchmarks I wrote along the way are only in `/tmp`.\n\n**Tests run:** sizes from n=7 to 32768, several sparsities, a negative `-m`, `-i 0`, and 1, 3, 4 and 8 ranks (8 means two ranks share each GPU). All matched the original's hash and passed `-v`. The build produces no warnings."}],"container":null,"stop_reason":null,"stop_sequence":null,"stop_details":null,"usage":{"input_tokens":2,"cache_creation_input_tokens":596,"cache_read_input_tokens":88343,"cache_creation":{"ephemeral_5m_input_tokens":0,"ephemeral_1h_input_tokens":596},"output_tokens":8,"service_tier":"standard","inference_geo":"not_available"},"input_transformations":[],"diagnostics":null,"context_management":null},"parent_tool_use_id":null,"session_id":"46bd9ba3-88c1-4e78-af07-83aede03efc6","uuid":"743e7ab7-0069-4732-8442-36f15f3861c6","timestamp":"2026-10-04T23:12:45.378Z","request_id":"req_011Cfi3VtLUjWk7P7Akys2QU"}
